options.systemMessage:
You are an estimating assistant for a general contractor. You read subcontractor bid quotes and compare them to open bid packages.

1. Call the Look Up Open Bid Packages tool first. It returns every open package with its package_code, project_name, trade and scope_checklist.
2. Decide if this email is a subcontractor quote for one of those packages. Match on project name, trade and scope. If it is not a quote, or no open package fits, set is_bid_quote to false and package_code to an empty string.
3. Extract the quote exactly as written. base_price is the total base bid as a plain number with no currency symbol or commas, excluding alternates. sub_contact_email is the estimator email printed on the quote, or an empty string if none is printed. validity_date uses YYYY-MM-DD or an empty string. Keep inclusions, exclusions, qualifications, alternates and addenda_acknowledged short and factual.
4. The scope_checklist is a list of item=allowance entries separated by semicolons. For EVERY checklist item, add one scope_coverage entry using the item text exactly as written, without the =allowance part. Use status included only if the quote clearly covers it, excluded if the quote excludes it or assigns it to others, and not_mentioned otherwise.
5. match_confidence is a number from 0 to 1 for the package match. Never invent prices, scope or dates.

  "base_price": 412500,
  "inclusions": "Supply and install 4 rooftop units, ductwork, duct insulation, testing and balancing, startup",
  "exclusions": "Controls and BAS, crane and rigging",

  "scope_coverage": [
    { "item": "Ductwork fabrication and install", "status": "included" },
    { "item": "Controls and BAS integration", "status": "excluded" }
  ],
  "reasoning": "Quote references the Riverside Medical Office Building HVAC package and its scope matches."
}

options.systemMessage: You are a senior construction estimator writing a short award recommendation for your project manager. The recommended subcontractor is always the lowest leveled total (base bid plus allowances for missing scope). Explain in plain text why it is the best value, compare it to the next lowest leveled bid, and list any risks to resolve before signing: expired or short price validity, unacknowledged addenda, qualifications, or exclusions the allowances may not fully cover. If a risk is serious enough that the estimator should not approve this award, say so clearly in the first sentence. Point out when the lowest base bid is not the lowest leveled bid. Keep it under 180 words, no headings, no markdown.

parameters.content:
## Level subcontractor bids and approve awards

### How it works

1. Subcontractors email their quotes. An AI agent reads each PDF, matches it to an open bid package in Data Tables, and marks every scope item as included, excluded or not mentioned.
2. Missing scope is priced at your allowance, so bids are compared on a leveled total instead of the headline number.
3. Subs with gaps are asked to confirm their exclusions. Unreadable files and unmatched emails follow their own paths.
4. A daily sweep reminds invited subs who have not bid, then closes bidding once the due date passes.
5. The AI recommends the lowest leveled bid, the estimator approves by email, and the winner and the other bidders are notified.

### Setup steps

- [ ] Connect your Gmail and OpenAI credentials.
- [ ] Run "Run Once: Set Up Bid Tables" once to create both Data Tables and a sample package.
- [ ] Add your packages to bid_packages, writing the scope checklist as Item=allowance; Item=allowance
- [ ] Set your company name and review inbox in the two settings nodes.
- [ ] Activate the workflow.

### Customization

Change the Gmail search query, the allowance amounts, the reminder timing, or how long the approval email waits before it times out.

## Create the bid tables

Run once to create the bid_packages and bid_quotes Data Tables with a sample package.

## Read and match incoming quotes

Each quote email is handled one at a time: the PDF text is extracted and an AI agent matches it to an open bid package.

## Level the quote against scope

Missing scope items are priced at your allowances and the quote is stored as the sub's latest revision.

## Reply to the subcontractor

Subs with scope gaps are asked to confirm their exclusions; complete quotes get a short receipt.

## Close bidding each morning

Loads every open package and locks the ones whose bid date has passed.

## Level and route each package

Ranks the package's quotes by leveled total and decides the next action.

## Chase bids and flag no-bids

Reminds invited subs who have not quoted and alerts the estimator when nobody bid.

## Recommend and approve the award

The AI writes an award recommendation and the estimator approves or holds it by email.

## Notify winner and other bidders

Sends the award intent to the winning sub and regret emails to everyone else.

## Narrow the Gmail search first

This workflow replies to senders automatically, so keep the trigger query tight enough that only real bid quotes match it.
